meta.title: Hush Studio Build Plan
meta.subtitle: Hush Studio: the recording and render app for the Sam Katz Hypnosis channel. Migrated 2026-11-10 from ops/state.json.

guide.heading: What this is
rows: Task plan for Hush Studio (sound recording app, repo folder pika_meditate). Narthen Control reads and edits this file.
CLAUDE.md is the architectural source of truth. Render speed is the #1 requirement: encode each unique piece once, build the long video by stream-copy.
Docs/Engine Build Plan/engine_plan.json (path kept from Narthen Control's defaults). The workbook is generated from it; never edit the .xlsx directly.

milestones.name: Fix recording quality
milestones.goal: Found in testing 2026-11-10: the audio sounds distorted and has cuts. Nothing else ships until a take records, masters and renders clean.
milestones.exit: Root causes found and fixed; an automated check catches clipping, distortion and dropouts; a real take is verified clean by ear and by test.

milestones.name: Verify and publish
milestones.goal: Prove the shipped pipeline on real material and publish to the real channel account.
milestones.exit: Full pytest green, FINISH timing on Sam's real take recorded, a real YouTube upload tested.

milestones.name: Editing workflow
milestones.goal: Sam can review and adjust everything the auto-editor proposes before render.
milestones.exit: Flub-cut proposals reviewable (accept/undo); induction-phase marker pauses handled.

milestones.name: Takes and editor
milestones.goal: After recording, an Edit button opens an Audacity-style editor so Sam can edit by hand or still use the automated features. Takes are saved, browsable, importable and exportable.
milestones.exit: Takes library with file-explorer view; import/export; in-app waveform editor; open in Audacity at any point.

milestones.name: Publishing and integrations
milestones.goal: Manage intros, set YouTube thumbnails, and connect Riverside and Canva.
milestones.exit: Intros can be uploaded and swapped; thumbnails upload with the video; Riverside and Canva workflows decided and built.

milestones.name: Install, update and diagnostics
milestones.goal: Sam installs the latest build with one download, the app updates itself from GitHub, and every problem she hits leaves logs (and, with her consent, audio) that we can debug from.
milestones.exit: A Setup.exe on GitHub Releases installs on a clean Windows PC; the app offers updates; a debug bundle from her PC can be opened with core.diagnostics.

milestones.name: Later scope
milestones.goal: Features deferred until the recording workflow is solid.

decisions.question: How should the hand-editor work?
decisions.options: Build our own waveform editor in the PyQt app; only hand off to Audacity; both.
decisions.recommendation: Both. A simple in-app editor (select, cut, delete, silence, undo, zoom, play, plus buttons for the automated features) so Sam never leaves the app, and an Open in Audacity round-trip for anything heavier.
decisions.outcome: 2026-11-10: Accepted the recommendation. Both. A simple in-app editor (select, cut, delete, silence, undo, zoom, play, plus buttons for the automated features) so Sam never leaves the app, and an Open in Audacity round-trip for anything heavier.

decisions.question: How deep should the Riverside integration go?
decisions.options: Drag/watch-folder import of Riverside exports; Riverside API (if her plan includes it); both.
decisions.recommendation: Start with a smooth import of Riverside exports (watch folder + drag-in, auto-detect 44.1 kHz mono). Add the API only if her plan exposes recording downloads.
decisions.outcome: 2026-11-10: let leave this feaute for a future update

decisions.question: How should Canva fit in?
decisions.options: Open Canva with a thumbnail template and import the exported PNG; Canva Connect API (OAuth, export design); both.
decisions.recommendation: Start with open-in-Canva plus importing the exported PNG from a watched folder. Connect API later if Sam wants one-click export from inside the app.
decisions.outcome: 2026-11-10: Accepted the recommendation. Start with open-in-Canva plus importing the exported PNG from a watched folder. Connect API later if Sam wants one-click export from inside the app.

decisions.question: Where do saved takes live, and what is a take?
decisions.options: Folder per take under a user-chosen Takes folder; single-file bundle; database index.
decisions.recommendation: Folder per take (raw audio, edit list, notes, metadata), in a Takes folder Sam can see in Explorer, with an exported .hushtake zip as the shareable form.
decisions.outcome: 2026-11-10: Accepted the recommendation. Folder per take (raw audio, edit list, notes, metadata), in a Takes folder Sam can see in Explorer, with an exported .hushtake zip as the shareable form.

decisions.question: Where do installable builds live, and does the source repo stay public?
decisions.options: Releases on the existing public Hush-Studio repo; a separate small public repo that holds only installers (source repo goes private); private repo plus an access token inside the app.
decisions.recommendation: A separate public repo for installers only (for example Hush-Studio-Releases), and make the source repo private. The updater then downloads anonymously with no token. Reason: the source repo is public today and its docs name Sam's channel and her home neighbourhood and default coordinates.
decisions.outcome: 2026-11-10: Accepted the recommendation. Installers are published in a separate public repo (Hush-Studio-Releases) that holds only builds; the source repo Hush-Studio becomes private. The updater downloads from the releases repo without a token.

decisions.question: How do logs and audio get from Sam's PC to us, and what audio may be captured?
decisions.options: Export a debug bundle zip that Sam sends herself (email or shared drive); upload to a private GitHub repo with a token; automatic upload.
decisions.recommendation: Export a zip she sends herself. Logs and measurements always; audio only as short clips around a problem spot, shown to her and sent only if she ticks a box. Her sessions are client-facing hypnosis recordings, so nothing leaves the PC without her choosing it.
decisions.outcome: 2026-11-10: Debug bundle is a zip Sam exports herself and hands over on a flash drive (email or a shared drive also fine). Logs and measurements always; audio only as opt-in clips she ticks. Nothing is uploaded automatically.

baseline: As recorded in CLAUDE.md section 0.6 (2026-11-09). Re-run under T6.

budget.plans: Claude and Codex subscription plans. Caps come from ops/state.json: 90% weekly, 95% five-hour.
tiers: Decisions and real-account tests that are yours

Near a usage limit, stop at a clean point and leave notes.

tasks.title: Find and fix the distorted audio in recorded takes
tasks.why: Reported from testing 2026-11-10: the output sounds distorted. Cause not yet known.
tasks.scope: Reproduce with a real mic take. Bisect the chain stage by stage (raw capture, denoise, auto-edit/splice, master gain and limiter, AAC encode) by listening to and measuring each stage's output (clipping, peak, THD, spectrum). Candidates to check, unconfirmed: input gain or clipping at capture, denoise artefacts, limiter or gain stage, crossfades at cuts, sample-rate mismatch. Fix the cause; do not mask it.
tasks.acceptance: A real take is clean at every stage and in the final MP4, confirmed by ear. The stage that introduced the distortion is named in the notes with before/after measurements.
tasks.verify: Per-stage measurements on a real take plus a listening check; tests added by T9.
tasks.notes: Reviewed claude/T7-find-and-fix-the-distorted-audio against main at c08936a. No correctness findings in denoise padding/context/scaling, capture clipping/overflow accounting, diagnostics, or UI warning changes. git diff --check clean. Review-only task; no code changes.

tasks.title: Find and fix the audio cuts (dropouts) in takes
tasks.why: Reported from testing 2026-11-10: there are cuts in the audio. Could be capture drops, plane-guard cuts, auto-edit, or the stitcher.
tasks.scope: Work out where the cuts come from: capture queue drops (the capture counter), plane-guard cut regions, auto-edit pause shaping, or seams in the stitched output. Compare the raw FLAC to the final output on the same take and locate each gap. Fix the cause. Surface any dropped-frame count in the UI so a bad take is obvious before FINISH.
tasks.acceptance: No unintended gaps in a real take's output. Dropped capture frames are counted and shown. Intentional cuts (plane cuts, pause shaping) are reviewable.
tasks.verify: Gap detection script over raw vs final on a real take; tests added by T9.
tasks.notes: Review clean: inspected core/capture.py loss accounting and timestamp resolution, capture.json totals versus capped/merged lost_at_s spots, UI wiring, and ReviewDialog playback for every retained spot including the 200-spot cap. Targeted T8 capture/UI tests passed (2); broader capture/UI run had 18 passed and 1 environment-only failure: DeepFilterNet coverage requires FFmpeg, which was unavailable.

tasks.title: Automated audio quality checks (clipping, distortion, dropouts)
tasks.why: The suite passed (171 tests) while real takes sounded distorted and had cuts. The tests did not cover real-signal quality.
tasks.scope: Add checks that run on a recorded or fixture speech take through the whole chain: clipped-sample count, peak and true-peak headroom, a distortion measure, and gap/dropout detection against the source. Fail the test and show a warning in the app on a bad take.
tasks.acceptance: Tests fail on a deliberately clipped or gapped input and pass on a clean one. A bad take shows a visible warning before FINISH.
tasks.verify: pytest tests -k quality
tasks.notes: Round-6 fixes: retain detached running quality QThreads until finished; use absolute full-scale clipping semantics with conservative analogue flat-top detection; suppress false Audacity unavailable banner; log worker exceptions; distinguish imported vs live advice when capture.json is missing; derive active frames from sample rate and remove redundant active pass; add quality worker and 3-arg prepare signal tests. Verified compileall, git diff --check, pytest tests -k quality: 11 passed. tasks.title: Open the audio in Audacity at any point, and bring the edits back
tasks.why: Sam wants to jump into Audacity at any stage for anything the app's editor does not do.
tasks.scope: Open in Audacity from the Takes screen, the editor and the review screen: export the current audio to a wav, launch Audacity on it (detect the install path), and include a label track for the cut and pause markers and the playhead position so the cursor opens where she was. After Audacity, offer Import changes to bring the exported file back as a new version of the take.
tasks.acceptance: From a take, Open in Audacity launches Audacity with the audio and markers. Importing the result back creates an updated take without losing the original.
tasks.verify: Manual with Audacity installed; pytest for the label export and import.
tasks.notes: Audacity has no command-line seek, so position is carried by a label track and the exported file, not a launch flag. Confirm at implementation time.

tasks.title: Intro manager: upload, replace and version intros
tasks.why: The intro card changes or gets updated. Sam must be able to upload a new one herself without touching files.
tasks.scope: An Intros screen: upload a video or image intro, preview it, name it, choose the active one, and keep older ones. Changing the active intro rebuilds the cached intro and black loop automatically (hash-keyed cache already exists). Validate resolution, frame rate and length, and show a clear message if the file is unsuitable.
tasks.acceptance: Upload a new intro, set it active, finish a take: the render uses it and the old one is still available. A bad file is rejected with an understandable message.
tasks.verify: pytest for cache rebuild on intro change; manual upload.
tasks.notes: Intro is a silent video card at the start of the video track; audio starts at t = 0 (see CLAUDE.md 0.5).

tasks.title: YouTube thumbnail: choose or upload one per video
tasks.why: Each upload needs a custom thumbnail; today the app has none.
tasks.scope: Pick or drop an image on the upload screen, validate it (16:9, 1280x720 recommended, under 2 MB, jpg or png), preview it, and send it with thumbnails.set after the video uploads. Remember a default thumbnail folder.
tasks.acceptance: An uploaded video shows the chosen thumbnail in YouTube Studio. A wrong-size or oversized image is flagged before upload.
tasks.verify: Tested against the fake server in tests; real account via T1.
tasks.notes: YouTube only allows custom thumbnails on verified channels; show that plainly if the call is refused.

tasks.title: Better Riverside integration
tasks.why: Sam records in Riverside and edits it, so getting Riverside takes into the app should be one step.
tasks.scope: At minimum: a watched Riverside download folder and drag-in that creates a take from a Riverside export (44.1 kHz mono, gated pauses, resample to 48 kHz on import). Extend to the Riverside API only if decision D02 says her plan supports it.
tasks.acceptance: A new Riverside export appears as a take with one click or automatically, ready to edit.
tasks.verify: Import a real Riverside export; pytest for the import conversion.
tasks.notes: Deferred by Sam (D02): leave Riverside integration for a future update.

tasks.title: Canva integration for thumbnails
tasks.why: Sam makes thumbnails in Canva. The app should shorten the trip from take to finished thumbnail.
tasks.scope: Per decision D03: Open in Canva (with her template link) from the upload screen, a watched export folder that offers the newest PNG as the thumbnail, and later the Canva Connect API if wanted.
tasks.acceptance: From the upload screen Sam opens Canva, exports, and the exported image is picked up as the thumbnail without manual file hunting.
tasks.verify: Manual run with a real Canva export.
tasks.notes: Canva Connect API needs OAuth and app approval; do not start it until D03 is decided.

tasks.title: Always-on logging: rotating log files, crash handler, system info
tasks.files: main.py, core/app_info.py, core/ (new logging setup), core/capture.py, core/renderer.py
tasks.why: To learn from takes recorded on Sam's PC we need to see what the app did. Today only capture.json exists per take.
tasks.scope: Set up Python logging once at startup: a rotating log file in the user's app-data folder (app, capture, denoise, render, upload), each line timestamped. Log app version, Windows version, Python/Qt/ffmpeg versions, audio devices and the chosen host API at start. Install a global exception hook that writes the traceback and shows a friendly message. Per-take: keep capture.json and stage diagnostics next to the take. Never log tokens, OAuth secrets or file contents.
tasks.acceptance: After a session and an induced error, the log shows what happened with timestamps, the versions, the mic in use, and the traceback. No secrets appear in it.
tasks.verify: pytest for the log setup and secret redaction; trigger a crash in a test build and read the log.
tasks.notes: core/log_setup.py: rotating log in %LOCALAPPDATA%\HushStudio\logs, redaction filter, startup versions/audio devices, global+thread excepthook with friendly dialog; log calls in capture/denoise/render/upload; wired in main.py. Verified: tests/test_log_setup.py (rotation, redaction, versions, induced crash in subprocess reads traceback from log); full pytest 216 passed.

tasks.title: Debug bundle: export logs, measurements and (opt-in) audio clips
tasks.files: ui/ (new Send debug report dialog), core/diagnostics.py, core/ (new bundle module)
tasks.why: When something sounds wrong on Sam's PC we need evidence we can open here, without asking her to dig through folders.
tasks.scope: A Help > Send debug report button that builds one zip: recent logs, system info, settings (secrets removed), and for the selected take its capture.json plus the per-stage report from core.diagnostics (peak, LUFS, clipping, dropouts at each stage). Audio is opt-in: show a list of short clips around flagged spots (clipping, dropouts) with a play button and a tick box per clip, nothing ticked by default, plus a plain note on what is included. The zip is saved to a chosen folder and its folder opened, so she can send it. Add `python -m core.diagnostics bundle.zip` to read a received bundle the same way as a session. Saving offers removable drives (a flash drive) first, and a Copy to flash drive shortcut, because that is how the bundle will reach us.
tasks.acceptance: Sam can produce a bundle in three clicks. With no boxes ticked it contains no audio. A bundle opened here prints the same stage report as a local session.
tasks.verify: pytest for the bundle contents and the no-audio default; manual: make and open a bundle.
tasks.notes: Help > Send debug report dialog (3 clicks: Help, Send debug report, Save). core/debug_bundle.py builds zip: logs, system, redacted settings, take capture.json + stage report; audio clips opt-in, none ticked by default; flash drives listed first + Copy to flash drive; python -m core.diagnostics bundle.zip prints same report. Verified: tests/test_debug_bundle.py (5 tests: contents, no-audio default, opt-in clip, bundle report == session report, dialog), full pytest 221 passed. Manual test with a real flash drive/real take not done.

tasks.title: Windows installer: Setup.exe that bundles everything Sam needs
tasks.files: build/ (PyInstaller spec, Inno Setup script), requirements.txt, core/ffmpeg_tools.py, config/
tasks.why: Sam should not install Python, FFmpeg or dependencies; she should double-click one file.
tasks.scope: Build the app with PyInstaller (one-folder), bundling Python, PyQt6, numpy/scipy, sounddevice, FFmpeg, deep-filter.exe, the Montserrat font, assets and config. Wrap it with Inno Setup into Hush-Studio-Setup-<version>.exe: per-user install (no admin), Start menu and desktop shortcut, uninstaller, keeps data and takes on upgrade. Settings, takes and logs live in the user's app-data folder, not the install folder. First run checks the microphone and tells her what to do if Windows blocks it. Check licences of everything bundled.
tasks.acceptance: On a clean Windows 10/11 PC (or fresh VM) with nothing installed, Setup.exe installs, the app records, renders and uploads, and uninstalling leaves her takes.
tasks.verify: Install on a clean VM; run the full flow; run the installer twice (upgrade) and confirm takes and settings survive.
tasks.notes: The installer will be unsigned, so Windows SmartScreen will warn (More info, then Run anyway). Code signing costs money; decide later. The same Setup.exe can be copied to a flash drive for an offline first install.

tasks.title: GitHub Actions: build and publish a release when a version is tagged
tasks.why: Releasing should be one step so Sam always has the latest build.
tasks.scope: Single version number in core/app_info.py. A workflow that runs on a version tag (v0.3.0) on a Windows runner: run the tests, build the installer (T21), and publish a GitHub Release with the Setup.exe, its SHA-256 and the changelog notes. Add a short RELEASING.md: bump version, tag, push. Where it publishes follows decision D05. Per D05 the workflow publishes the Release to the separate public Hush-Studio-Releases repo (the private source repo cannot serve anonymous downloads). That needs a fine-grained GitHub token limited to the releases repo, stored as an Actions secret in the source repo.
tasks.acceptance: Pushing a tag produces a Release with a working Setup.exe and checksum, with no manual build.
tasks.verify: Tag a pre-release and download and run the installer.

tasks.title: In-app updater: check GitHub for a newer version and install it
tasks.why: Sam should get new builds without hunting for downloads.
tasks.scope: On start (and from a Check for updates button) ask the Releases API for the latest version without any login. If newer, show What's new and an Update now button that downloads the Setup.exe, verifies its SHA-256, runs it silently, and reopens the app. Never update while recording or rendering. Fail quietly when offline. Allow skipping a version. It reads releases from the Hush-Studio-Releases repo (D05).
tasks.acceptance: With an older build installed and a newer release published, the app offers the update and ends up on the new version with her takes and settings intact. Offline start shows no error.
tasks.verify: Test with a fake releases endpoint; manual upgrade from an older installer.
